ui.prompt.intro: I am studying courses in the Lectorea catalogue ({site}) — open video lectures arranged in the order you learn them, each course belonging to a field of knowledge. Below: what is behind me, what I am in the middle of and what I have marked as a favourite; under each course are the playlists I watched it by.
ui.prompt.nothing: No course has been marked yet.
ui.prompt.watched: Watched in all: about {hours} h, {lectures} lectures marked.
ui.prompt.weekGoal: This week: {hours} h against a goal of {goal} h.
ui.prompt.ask: Draw up a study plan for me: what to take next given what is behind me and what I have marked, in what order, and why. Suggest further material — textbooks, problem sets, lecture notes — to close the gaps. Ask me anything you are missing.
ui.continent.formal.desc: Mathematics, logic and the natural sciences. A claim is accepted once it has been proved or reproduced in an experiment — and anyone can check it again
ui.continent.social.desc: People and society: economics, sociology, psychology, law. They lean on data and statistics too, but what they study changes because it is being studied
ui.continent.humanities.desc: What people have made: languages, texts, art, religion, the past. The argument is about the source and how it is read, not about an experiment
ui.map.legend: Three continents — three branches of knowledge; inside a continent, the more courses a field has, the more room it takes
ui.column.legend: Columns go by difficulty: the further right a course sits, the longer the chain you have to work through to reach it
ui.column.legendSelected: “{course}” is selected — its chain of prerequisites and what it opens up next are lit; everything else is dimmed
ui.graph.empty: No courses under the current filters
ui.legend.title: What is what here
ui.legend.level: Column number: how many courses the longest path to this place goes through
ui.legend.levelGroup: Group number: how many courses the longest path to this place goes through
ui.legend.playlistCount: How many playlists were found for the course
ui.legend.dimmed: A dimmed card is outside the selected course's chain. It is still clickable
ui.legend.inPath: The course is part of the selected one's chain of prerequisites
ui.legend.done: The course is marked as done
ui.legend.inProgress: The course is marked as started — you are studying it now
ui.legend.favorite: The course is a favourite — and a goal in your profile
ui.legend.stage: When this course is usually taken: a school year or a university year
ui.legend.hours: Roughly how many hours the course takes
ui.legend.domain: The field the course belongs to — opens the catalogue of that field
ui.legend.quality: Playlist quality: high, average, little data
ui.legend.playlistType: What the recording is: a shelf on a subject, seminars, or a whole course. Not a verdict — the verdict is on the right
ui.legend.noMaterials: The course is in the catalogue, but no playlists have been found for it yet
ui.legend.guest: A field tag on the artwork means a course from another field, kept in the columns while you are reading it — or while the chain of the selected course runs through it; pressing it moves you to that field along with the course

ui.playlist.statusHow: Where does the status come from?
ui.playlist.status.sparse.hint: Too few views to conclude anything: one chance wave of interest would move any score
ui.playlist.status.fresh.hint: The last lecture went up recently — the numbers are still settling
ui.playlist.status.excellent.hint: Above the catalogue on two independent counts at once: people both like it and watch it through
ui.playlist.status.retained.hint: Noticeably more viewers are still there for the last lectures than usual: the course holds them
ui.playlist.status.liked.hint: More likes per view than its contemporaries in the same language
ui.playlist.status.discussed.hint: Noticeably more comments per view than usual: people argue and work through it under the lectures rather than just watching
ui.playlist.status.reaching.hint: Far more views per lecture than the channel has subscribers: it is watched well beyond its own audience
ui.playlist.status.classic.hint: Recorded years ago and people are still finding and watching it
ui.playlist.ratingTooltip: Sorted by a combined score: likes per view, and the share of viewers who make it to the end. Both are measured against the catalogue — against contemporaries in the same language, because a like in 2010 was worth a third of one today
ui.playlist.retentionValue: ~{percent} of those who start reach the end
ui.playlist.noStatusHint: Nothing stands out among its contemporaries — but the data says nothing bad about it either
ui.playlist.relativeHint: The scale is relative: it shows this metric against the other playlists in the catalogue, not as a share of anything

ui.home.title: Your learning

ui.profile.data.promptHint: The prompt is the same thing in words, with nothing extra: the courses are named rather than encoded. Hand it to your AI agent and it will see what you have already covered — enough to draw up a study plan of your own or to find further material

ui.playlist.type.course.hint: A whole course: a dozen sessions or more, filmed over one period, all the same length with none of them the odd one out. It says nothing about quality — only that the course is complete
ui.playlist.type.uneven.hint: One lecture in ten or more is nothing like the rest: ten-minute ones next to ninety-minute ones. Not a shelf but a course, and no two sittings are alike — its «average lecture» says little
ui.playlist.type.seminars.hint: Problem sessions rather than lectures: that is what most of the recordings inside call themselves
ui.playlist.type.collection.hint: Not a course but a shelf on a subject: views do not fall off along the order, and it shows how it was put together — over years, in unequal lengths, unnumbered. People arrive at these from search, anywhere in the middle

ui.course.recommendsHint: Not required: the course works without it, but reads better with it. Not counted in the path or the hours.
link.genetics.probability: Segregation and linkage are probability calculations; without them Mendel's laws are rules to memorise.
link.ecology.statistics: Abundances and community links are estimated from samples — without statistics they are noise.
link.analytical-chemistry.statistics: Error, confidence interval and limit of detection are the language every analysis reports in.
link.cognitive-science-intro.linguistics: Language is cognitive science's main proving ground; half the examples are about it.
link.functional-programming.category-the: Functors, monads and their laws are named after category theory, which is where the names come from.
link.software-engineering.databases: Almost every project the course dissects stores state; schemas and transactions make the examples real.
link.signal-processing.probability: Noise and spectral density are described as a random process rather than a clean signal.
link.robotics.programming-intro: Control here is written as code; without programming the practical half is out of reach.
link.numerical-methods.programming-intro: A method only exists once it is coded; the course is checked by running it.
link.numerical-methods.differential-equa: Half the methods are numerical ODE solvers; MIT makes differential equations a hard prerequisite.
link.cell-biology.organic-chemistry: Functional groups explain why a membrane holds together and why a protein folds the way it does.
link.evolution.statistics: Population genetics is estimating allele frequencies and testing hypotheses about them.
link.neuroscience.biochemistry: A synapse is receptors, second messengers and ion pumps — biochemistry all the way down.
link.biochemistry.thermodynamics: Every "why does this reaction go" in the course is a free-energy argument.
link.immunology.molecular-biology: Antibody gene rearrangement and antigen presentation are read through transcription and translation.
link.epidemiology.microbiology: The machinery is statistical, but what it counts are pathogens and the ways they travel.
link.bioinformatics-intro.statistics: The significance of an alignment is statistics; without it a hit is indistinguishable from chance.
link.physical-chemistry.quantum-mechanic: Spectra and molecular structure are quantum arguments; otherwise they stay empirical rules.
link.astrophysics.quantum-mechanics: Stellar spectra, fusion in cores and degeneracy pressure are all quantum arguments.
link.geochemistry.thermodynamics: Mineral equilibria and phase diagrams are chemical thermodynamics applied directly.
link.climatology.statistics: A climate is a statistic about weather, and the argument about trends is made in estimation.
link.historical-geology.evolution: Strata are dated by fossils, and faunal turnover is read as an evolutionary sequence.
link.databases.operating-systems: Buffer pools, pages and the write-ahead log are the memory and disk work a systems course teaches.
link.cryptography.probability: Security is stated as a claim about probabilities: the cipher is indistinguishable from randomness.
link.digital-logic.discrete-math: Gates are Boolean algebra with a soldering iron; the course starts from scratch, but discrete maths shows why.
link.ml-intro.statistics: Probability is the gate; estimation and confidence intervals separate reading a metric from believing it.
link.nlp.linguistics-intro: The models work on morphology, syntax and meaning — the terms linguistics defines.
link.econometrics.linear-algebra: Regression is taught twice, in sums and in matrix form; the second telling is the one that generalises.
link.finance.random-processes: Prices are modelled as random processes; without them options are formulas with no derivation.
link.computational-linguistics-intro.sta: Distributional methods and parser evaluation both rest on statistics.
link.psychology-intro.neuroscience: The same behaviour from two sides: psychology describes it from outside, neuroscience from within.
link.social-psychology.sociology-intro: The group seen from the person and the person seen from the group — two halves of one subject.
link.anthropology-intro.archaeology-intr: One discipline, two sources: living people for the anthropologist, their things for the archaeologist.
link.nlp.computational-linguistics-intro: One task from two sides: engineering starts from models, linguistics from the structure of language.
link.cryptography.information-theory: Shannon's perfect secrecy is an information-theoretic theorem, and every security claim starts there.
link.computability.theory-of-computation: Neighbouring courses on one question: what a machine can do at all, and what it costs.
link.epidemiology.demography: Both count populations — cases here, births and deaths there — with methods from the same family.
link.climatology.ecology: Climate sets the frame ecosystems live in, and ecosystems put carbon back into the climate.
link.archaeology-intro.historical-geolog: Stratigraphy is shared: layers, dating and the law of superposition read the same in both.
link.marketing.social-psychology: Choice, influence and group norms: marketing applies what social psychology measures.
link.human-resource-management.labour-la: Hiring, firing and working time: the practice runs into the law, and the law is written for the practice.
link.law-intro.political-science-intro: The state from two sides: legal norms and political institutions describe one arrangement.
link.music-history.art-history-intro: The styles move together: baroque, classicism and modernism are recognisable in both arts.
link.pedagogy-intro.developmental-psycho: What to teach and when: developmental psychology describes the ages the teaching is aimed at.
link.systematic-theology.medieval-philos: Scholasticism is shared ground: the same texts and the same disputes about universals.
ui.course.relatedHint: Neither a prerequisite nor a sequel: a neighbouring subject looking at the same thing from another side. Order does not matter.
link.cultural-anthropology.sociology-int: Society and culture, one subject from two traditions: one counts institutions, the other describes meanings.
link.archaeology-intro.ancient-history: Written sources and material ones: one era, two kinds of evidence that check each other.
link.ancient-art.archaeology-intro: Vase painting, sculpture and layout come out of excavations; attribution without archaeology is guesswork.
link.renaissance-art.medieval-history: Patrons, guilds and cities explain why Renaissance painting looks the way it does.
link.classical-philology.ancient-literat: Philology reads the same texts as literature, but asks about the language rather than the meaning.
link.history-of-science-intro.philosophy: How science changed and what counts as knowledge: the historian answers with facts, the philosopher with criteria.
link.historiography.philosophy-of-scienc: Both ask how the historian knows: one studies the craft, the other the justification.
link.semantics.mathematical-logic: Formal semantics is models and truth in them — the apparatus of mathematical logic.
link.sociolinguistics.sociology-intro: Speech as a social marker: language variables and social variables are measured together.
link.human-geography-intro.sociology-int: Settlement, migration and cities: geography gives social processes their space.
link.urban-studies.sociology-intro: The city belongs to both: layout and segregation are described together.
link.film-studies-intro.art-history-intr: The frame inherits composition and light from painting, and is read with the same notions.
link.logic-intro.philosophy-intro: Argument and inference: logic formalises what philosophy uses on every page.
link.poetics.linguistics-intro: Metre, rhyme and tropes are described linguistically; poetics speaks phonetics and syntax.
link.ancient-literature.ancient-history: Homer and tragedy are read inside their own city; without history the plots have no audience.
link.international-law.international-rel: Treaties and wars: law describes the norms, international relations how they are actually kept.
link.ancient-philosophy.ancient-history: Socrates and the polis: philosophy answers its own city's questions, not questions in general.
link.medieval-philosophy.religious-studi: Theology and philosophy in the Middle Ages are one discussion: the same texts, authors and disputes.
link.ethics.political-philosophy: What is just for a person and what for a state: one question at two scales.
link.epistemology.logic-intro: Knowledge, justification and inference: epistemology argues about what logic formalises.
link.philosophy-of-language.semantics: The meaning of a word: philosophy asks what it is, semantics how to write it down.
link.ethnomusicology.cultural-anthropolo: Music as custom: recording and analysing a song is an anthropologist's fieldwork.
link.international-relations.modern-hist: The twentieth-century order is explained by its wars; the theory without that record floats free.
link.social-theory.philosophy-intro: Durkheim, Weber and Marx belong to both; the argument about society starts in philosophy.
link.biblical-studies.ancient-history: The biblical text is a source for ancient Near Eastern history, and the other way round.
link.probability.combinatorics: Computing probabilities means counting outcomes; combinations are needed from the first problem.
link.random-processes.measure-theory: Continuous time needs a rigorous measure; without one the definition of a process falls into paradoxes.
link.differential-equations.linear-algeb: Systems and the stability of solutions are the eigenvalues of a matrix, not a separate theory.
link.game-theory.probability: A mixed strategy is a distribution, and equilibrium is found in expected payoffs.
link.microeconomics.calculus-1: Marginal utility and marginal cost are derivatives; the whole optimisation rests on them.
link.econometrics.microeconomics: What is estimated is not any correlation but the parameters of the behaviour models micro sets up.
link.ml-intro.linear-algebra: The data here are matrices and learning is operations on them: projections, decompositions, gradients.
link.deep-learning.optimization: Training a network is constrained gradient descent; without optimisation it stays magic.
link.reinforcement-learning.random-proce: The environment is modelled as a Markov process; without it there is no state and no value.
link.computer-graphics.linear-algebra: Camera, rotation and projection are matrix multiplications; graphics is linear algebra in real time.
link.cryptography.number-theory: RSA and Diffie-Hellman live in modular arithmetic; without it they are incantations.
link.signal-processing.calculus-3: The Fourier transform is an integral one: multiple integrals and a word about convergence are needed.
link.numerical-methods.linear-algebra: Almost every problem reduces to solving a system, and a method's stability is a property of the matrix.
link.statistical-physics.probability: An ensemble is a distribution and entropy is computed over it; thermodynamics follows from statistics.
link.complex-analysis.real-analysis: Analyticity is differentiability strengthened; limits and convergence are needed in rigorous form.
link.functional-analysis.measure-theory: Function spaces are built on the Lebesgue integral; without measure there is no completeness and no L².
link.general-relativity.differential-geo: Gravity is curvature: the metric, the connection and the curvature tensor are introduced there.
link.model-theory.abstract-algebra: The examples of theories and their models are groups, fields and rings; without them the course is empty.
link.theory-of-computation.mathematical-: Undecidability is proved with logic: formalisation, coding and the diagonal argument.
link.data-structures.discrete-math: Complexity bounds and correctness proofs are induction, graphs and sums — discrete maths.
link.computer-architecture.digital-logic: The course opens on gates and flip-flops and never teaches them; that is the course before it.
link.compilers.computer-architecture: Code generation and register allocation are aimed at a particular machine.
link.compilers.theory-of-computation: Lexing and parsing are automata and grammars; the front end is built straight on them.
link.cell-biology.general-chemistry: Membranes, gradients and pH are chemistry; without bonding and solutions the course is a set of pictures.
link.molecular-biology.genetics: Regulation is explained through mutants and crosses; genetics gives the language for «what broke».
link.inorganic-chemistry.organic-chemist: The chemistry of the elements is read in terms of bonding, orbitals and mechanism that organic sets up.
link.electrodynamics.oscillations-waves: Maxwell ends in the wave equation, which by that point has to be something you can already solve.
link.geophysics.differential-equations: Seismology and gravimetry are boundary-value problems for partial differential equations.
link.ocean-engineering.transport-phenome: Wave loads are computed from hydrodynamics, whose core is momentum transport.
link.quantum-mechanics.analytical-mechan: The Hamiltonian comes from analytical mechanics and stays the course's main object.
link.physical-chemistry.thermodynamics: Chemical equilibrium is a free-energy minimum; the apparatus is taken ready-made.
link.epidemiology.statistics: Risk, odds ratios and confidence intervals are what every conclusion in the course is made of.
link.bioinformatics-intro.algorithms: Alignment is dynamic programming; searching a database is indexes and trees.
link.metrology.probability: An error is a random variable; without distributions it can be neither added up nor estimated.
link.geodesy.statistics: Coordinates are not measured but estimated; adjusting a network is least squares.
link.historical-geology.general-biology: Strata are dated by the remains of organisms; you have to know who they were and how they differ.
link.bioethics-intro.ethics: The argument about what is permissible is made in normative theories, not in intuitions.
link.psych-research-methods.statistics: Experimental design and hypothesis testing are one discipline seen from two sides.
link.demography.social-research-methods: Censuses and samples are the data source, and how they are built decides what can be counted at all.
link.corpus-linguistics.statistics: Frequencies, collocations and the significance of differences are statistical estimates over a corpus.
link.computational-linguistics-intro.syn: A parser recovers the structure syntax describes; without it there is nothing to program.
link.cognitive-science-intro.neuroscienc: Models of cognition are checked against how the brain is built; otherwise they are metaphors.
link.operations-management.optimization: Schedules, inventories and routes are linear and integer programming problems.
link.pharmacology.biochemistry: What a drug does is bind to a protein and interfere with a metabolic pathway.
link.immunology.microbiology: Immunity is studied against particular pathogens; you have to know them by name.
link.control-theory.differential-equatio: Stability and transient response are properties of the solutions of a linear system.
link.meteorology.thermodynamics: Convection, humidity and clouds are the thermodynamics of moist air.
link.transport-phenomena.thermodynamics: Fluxes run against gradients, and the gradients themselves are set by equilibrium thermodynamics.
link.astrophysics.thermodynamics: A star is a balance of pressure and gravity; without thermodynamics there is no model and no spectrum.
link.cosmology.general-relativity: Expansion is a solution of Einstein's equations; without them Friedmann comes from nowhere.
link.historiography.modern-history: The argument about method is made on real material; it needs a body of events to argue about.
link.economic-history.econ-intro: The past is analysed with market models; without them it is a chronicle of prices.
link.abstract-algebra.linear-algebra: Groups and rings generalise what is already visible in matrices and vector spaces.
link.category-theory.topology: The first substantial examples are homotopies and sheaves; without topology the definitions are empty.
link.set-theory.mathematical-logic: Axioms and independence are stated as claims about derivability.
link.field-archaeology.geodesy: The excavation grid, find coordinates and site plan are surveying at an archaeological scale.
link.bioethics-intro.law-intro: Patient consent, capacity and the limits of intervention are at once ethical questions and legal rules.
link.information-theory.signal-processin: Entropy sets the limits of compression and transmission; signal processing shows how real data can approach them.
link.ml-intro.econometrics: Both build models from data: machine learning puts prediction first, econometrics causal explanation and parameter estimation.
link.computer-vision.optics: Lenses, projection and exposure explain how an image is formed before an algorithm begins to interpret it.
link.computer-vision.computer-graphics: Vision recovers a scene from an image while graphics makes an image from a scene; they share camera geometry.
link.reinforcement-learning.control-theo: Both choose actions over time: control starts from a model of the system, reinforcement learning learns through interaction.
link.behavioral-economics.cognitive-psyc: Limited attention, memory and heuristics are the psychological machinery behind the departures from rational choice that behavioural economics measures.
link.international-relations.game-theory: Deterrence, commitment and bargaining become games when the outcome depends on the other side's next move.
link.geodesy.linear-algebra: Changing coordinate systems and adjusting a survey network are matrix transformations and systems of linear equations.
link.project-management.software-enginee: Estimation, risk and iteration become concrete in software projects, while engineering practices depend on managing the whole project.
link.ocean-engineering.oceanography: Oceanography describes waves, currents and the seabed; ocean engineering turns that environment into loads and design constraints.
